_note: One-time plain-English translations of the legacy free-text proposals (0 to 15). The chain text is unchanged; the page shows these in place of the raw text with the raw text one click away. Written by Wren, 2026-09-17.

0.title: Stop the test suite going red when the widget is busy
0.summary: One safety test checks that no test writes to real files by comparing timestamps before and after. When the live widget writes its own files mid-run, the test fails for the wrong reason and someone has to re-run it. This makes the test check whether the widget is busy first, or compare file contents rather than timestamps.
0.why: A false failure costs a re-run most sessions and teaches people to ignore red.
0.technical: test_zz_no_real_state_written: an idle precheck on the widget, or fingerprint by shape rather than mtime.

1.title: One shared cache helper instead of four copies
1.summary: Four parts of the widget each keep their own copy of the same small caching code, which re-reads a file only when it changed. This merges them into one shared helper so a bug fixed once is fixed everywhere.
1.why: Four copies drift; a caching bug would hit one and hide in the other three.
1.technical: mtime_cache(path, build) shared by citations, gates, precedents and kayako_client; removes about 80 lines.

2.title: Catch mangled code before it is committed
2.summary: Three times this week a script written through the shell turned a text pattern into an invisible control character, breaking a check silently. This adds an automatic pre-commit scan that refuses any widget file containing such characters.
2.why: The bug is invisible to the eye and was found three times by accident.
2.technical: pre-commit grep for chr(8) and other control characters in tools/floating-assistant/*.py.

3.title: The validators should agree on what the ticket is about
3.summary: Three checks each build their own picture of the current ticket from the ledger, in slightly different ways, so they can disagree on the same answer. This gives them one shared picture.
3.why: Disagreement between checks produced confusing rejections.
3.technical: one turn_context() in output_validator used by check_citations, check_macro_names and check_gates.

4.title: Fewer lines scrolling past at the start of each turn
4.summary: Turn one prints eight status lines for its preparation steps. This collapses them into one line with the detail one click away.
4.why: The operator scrolls past them every turn; the detail is rarely needed.
4.technical: pre-turn stream lines collapsed to 'pre-turn: 8 steps, 2 notes' with detail on click.

5.title: Record which widget version worked each ticket
5.summary: Nothing today records which version of the widget produced a case page or a thread. This stamps the version into both so any regression can be traced to a release.
5.why: Without it a later problem cannot be tied to the release that caused it.
5.technical: widget_version field in the caselog header and on the thread.

6.title: Check macro names against Kayako every day
6.summary: The report that finds stale macro names in the knowledge base found 47 in twenty seconds. This runs it every day at idle instead of only inside the full weekly review.
6.why: Cheap, writes nothing, and keeps the articles honest.
6.technical: macro_audit on a daily idle schedule.

7.title: One rule for hiding secrets everywhere
7.summary: Three different parts of the widget each decide on their own what counts as a password or token to hide. This puts the rule in one place so it cannot drift.
7.why: Never printing a credential should be one rule, not three.
7.technical: shared redact.py used by postman_client, permission_gate and metis_ask.

8.title: Show what a Postman edit would change before approving it
8.summary: When the widget asks permission to edit a Postman request, the approval card shows a sentence, not the change itself. This shows the changed request beside the current one.
8.why: Approval should be given on what actually changes.
8.technical: diff view on the approval card for put_request.

9.title: Pin the test-runner version for Postman runs
9.summary: Each Postman run downloads the runner afresh, so an approved run depends on the network and could change under you. This pins the version and names it on the approval card.
9.why: An approved action should be reproducible.
9.technical: pinned newman version in the npx call, shown on the card.

10.title: Save every Postman run to the ticket's case page
10.summary: A Postman run's result lands in the chat thread but not on the ticket's case page. This would add it there as a section.
10.why: So the next person reading the case sees what was sent to the test system.
10.technical: ===POSTMAN RUN=== block written as a caselog section.

11.title: Tidy the tray menu into groups
11.summary: The tray menu has eleven items mixing switches and panels, and the new Postman item hides among them. This groups them into State, Panels and Session.
11.why: One commit, no risk, easier to find things.
11.technical: tray items grouped into three sections.

12.title: Capture the 90 articles the knowledge base links to but lacks
12.summary: A new report names exactly which linked articles are missing from the brain: 43 in Khoros Classic, 24 in Alpha, 23 in Kayako. This captures just those instead of re-syncing everything.
12.why: Closes the training gap cheaply and precisely.

13.title: Never measure a page's footnotes as its content
13.summary: The new 'Linked articles' section at the end of each article was being counted as part of the article's body by some checks, which broke one of them. This gives every check one shared way to read the body without such sections.
13.why: The same mistake will recur wherever a page's text is measured.
13.technical: page_body() strips metadata sections before verbatim_fragment, page_text scoring and search_symptom.

14.title: Do not summarise articles from a cut-off copy
14.summary: The sync summarises long articles from their first 12,000 characters while treating anything over 11,000 as long, so mid-sized articles are summarised from a truncated copy. This lines the two numbers up.
14.why: A silent truncation loses content nobody notices.
14.technical: raise the distillation slice to the verbatim threshold in kba_sync.

15.title: Keep the linked-articles lists current automatically
15.summary: The one-off job that adds a 'Linked articles' list to every article takes under two minutes. This runs it at the end of every sync so the lists stay current as articles change.
15.why: No operator step, and the lists never go stale.
15.technical: D56 backfill at the end of each kba_sync run.
